newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Weathery teas depress prices at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Weathery teas depress prices at Colombo auction.

text.p: Monsoon-boosted quantities and a general lowering of quality kept prices depressed at the Colombo tea auction where 5.1 million kg were on offer, brokers said on Wednesday.
The island's distinct low-grown teas, popular with Russian and Middle Eastern buyers, held firm, but the more pricey high-growns declined due to poor quality, they said.
"Low growns did well despite larger weights available in the market," said a broker with Eastern Brokers. "But most high-growns eased due to weather-related lowering in quality."
Brokers said it was customary for quantity to increase and quality to drop when the monsoon rains set in.
"With monsoonal teas coming in, prices would tend to come down a little in the next few weeks," the broker said.
The CIS, Turkey and Saudi Arabia were active buyers of low-growns while Britain, South Africa and Japan bought highs more selectively, brokers Forbes and Walker said.
The anticipated gross auction average was 112.75 rupees ($1.92) per kg, as compared to 114.89 last week, Forbes said.
The next auction, where five million kg will be on offer, will be limited to one day due to a Buddhist holiday next week.
